text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 1801: KV cache memory spike on hosted-runtime-us-east-1 -> paging to incidents channel. priority: P1. Affected service: runtime.kv-cache.
oncall-bot: Pager: high OOM rate in kvcache shards, autoscaler kicking but pods failing with OOMKilled.
sanjay: Seeing sustained growth in kv_entries_per_shard metric, looks like a runaway context window. Heap growth correlates with large prompt sizes from a single customer.
maria: Confirmed. Customer 'acme-inc' sent multi-megabyte system prompt via streaming API. k/v store retained prefixes because eviction policy didn't account for multi-turn retention.
ashley: Are we seeing continuous batching causing delays in eviction? Could batching be keeping large KV references alive?
sanjay: Yes — continuous batching collects prefixes into in-flight batches. Batches are pinned until the KV flush deadline, combining with kvcache prefetch to amplify retention.
kevin: Dumped a heap profile: top entries are kv_blob_* for model-redwood-13b, mostly 3-5MB blobs. Attachments: stack traces show gc not reclaiming due to references.
maria: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Disable prefetch on hosted runtime for model-redwood-13b. 2) Temporarily cap max_kv_blob_size and force eviction of blobs > 256KB. 3) Reduce continuous_batch_window_ms to 10ms. 4) Scale up runtime pool by +2 nodes while fixing config.
sanjay: Executing step 1 now -> posting command to disable prefetch on fleet: 
```
# apply temporary feature-flag via chef/infra
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/flags -d '{"service":"hosted-runtime-us-east-1","flag":"kvcache_prefetch","value":false}'
```
ops-bot: Flag change rolled out to 8/10 hosts, circuit ok.
kevin: Pushing eviction patch to canary group (2 hosts): 
```
# runtime config patch
kvcache:
  max_blob_size_bytes: 262144
  eviction_policy: lru_age_preference
```
sanjay: Canary looks good, memory usage down ~30% on those hosts. No request errors observed aside from a few delayed responses.
ashley: Lowering continuous_batch_window_ms on all hosted runtime pools now. Command: `kubectl patch config hosted-runtime -p '{"spec":{"continuousBatchWindowMs":10}}'`
deploy-bot: Rolling patch applied to 6/10 pods; will finish in 2 minutes.
maria: We should notify support and impacted customers. @support-team please prepare a short advisory: "We observed degraded performance due to unusually long prompts; mitigations are active."
jordan: I'm drafting the advisory and will post to status.redwood.ai after we verify stability for 15 mins.
kevin: After full rollout (10/10 hosts) memory trends normalized. Autoscaler no longer firing. Error rate returned to baseline.
sanjay: Marking immediate incident state: mitigated. Root cause hypothesis: client-side long system prompts + continuous batching pinned large KV blobs causing retention beyond expected TTL; eviction heuristics didn't cap blob size leading to OOM.
maria: Next actions for follow-up: 1) enforce global max_kv_blob_size in config (not just canary). 2) Add quota on prompt payload size for hosted plans. 3) Instrument batch pinning lifetime metric and add alert if pinned_blob_mem > 200MB per shard. 4) Postmortem owner: kevin + maria.
ashley: I'll file the rollback/hardening PR with tests for max_blob_size and batch window guardrails.
jordan: Handoff to next on-call (samar) at 1801234987. Samar, current state: mitigations applied, system stable, follow-ups assigned to kevin/maria/ashley. See thread for commands and diagnostics.
onspecific-note: Reaction emojis: :white_check_mark: on mitigations, :memo: on postmortem assignment.
onspecific-note: No customer data exposed in logs shared in thread.
